new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the first syllable of the phonological word and is non-contrastive. Clitics and affixes carry no stress of their own; enclitics leave initial stress on the host; a (C)V pronominal proclitic joins the host's phonological word without attracting stress, so stress stays on the host's first syllable (= second syllable of the clitic group). A proclitic or VP particle that forms a phonological word on its own is stressed on its first syllable.
new_statements.secondary_stress: No secondary stress described as such; reduplicated forms consist of two phonological words, each stressed on its first syllable (e.g. ['toru'toruru] 'round'); compounds take a single stress on the first syllable of the whole word.
new_statements.exceptions: Proclitic + host groups surface with stress on the second syllable of the phonological word (first syllable of the host); diphthongs carry prominence on the first element; footnote in the valency chapter (thesis fn. 63) speculates without evidence that a CVC object proclitic might affect host stress.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (host plus clitics), explicitly distinguished from the grammatical word; examples are citation forms and textual examples with stress marks. Intonational 'strong stress' on linking adverbials (sainio, soinio) is treated separately under intonation/discourse.
new_statements.identity_note: Obata's grammar describes Bilua (blb, bilu1245) as spoken on Vella Lavella, Western Province, Solomon Islands (fieldwork 1990s); no dialect split is made for the stress statement. The 2000 ANU thesis and the 2003 Pacific Linguistics book carry identical wording for section 2.5.

sources.note: Ch. 2 sec. 2.5 (p. 12): stress falls on the first syllable of the phonological word; not contrastive; on a diphthong realised on the first element. Sec. 2.6 (pp. 12-14): clitics and affixes bear no inherent stress; proclitics do not shift stress off the host, so a proclitic+host phonological word is stressed on its second syllable (first of the host); VP particles or proclitics forming their own phonological word take initial stress; reduplicants are separate phonological words each with initial stress; compounds carry one initial stress.
